## Owner Safe Pets 1.0

First release.

- Tamed wolves, cats, parrots, horses, donkeys, mules, llamas and camels take no damage from the player who tamed them.
- This covers direct hits, sword sweeps, arrows, tridents and other projectiles you shot, and explosions you caused, such as TNT you lit.
- A sitting wolf or parrot stays seated when you hit it by mistake.
- Damage from anyone or anything else is unchanged.
- Only the server needs the mod: players without it are covered too.

## Owner Safe Pets 1.1

Settings.

- New file `config/ownersafepets.json`, created on the first start. Without changes everything works exactly like 1.0.
- `sneakToHit` (default `false`): set it to `true` and you can hurt your own pet while sneaking, for example to put down a sick animal. Only your own hits count; your arrows and explosions stay harmless to your pets.
- `protectFromOwnerExplosions` (default `true`): set it to `false` and TNT you lit or crystals you hit can hurt your pets again.
- A broken value falls back to its default with a warning in the server log.
- Everything from 1.0 stays the same.

## Owner Safe Pets 1.2

Your own potions spare your pets.

- Splash and lingering potions you throw no longer give your tamed animals harmful effects: no poison, weakness, slowness or any other harmful effect. This also covers the cloud a lingering potion leaves behind. (Harming potions already did no damage to your pets.)
- Helpful effects still work: a healing or regeneration potion you throw at your pet heals it as before. A mixed potion such as turtle master gives your pet the resistance but not the slowness.
- Your pet no longer uses up your own harmful lingering cloud while it stands in it, so the cloud lasts as long as it would without the pet.
- Potions thrown by other players, witches or dispensers are unchanged.
- New setting `protectFromOwnerPotions` in `config/ownersafepets.json` (default `true`). Set it to `false` and your potions affect your pets as in vanilla. Config files from 1.1 keep working; without the setting the default is used. `sneakToHit` still only concerns your own hits.
- Everything from 1.1 stays the same.
